implementationStrengths: Dependency-free Node ESM CLI (create/validate/status) runs directly with Node built-ins; no root package.json introduced.
Package validator is broad and correct on the core cases (encoding, inventory, manifest byte+hash, unique/typed IDs, dangling refs, symlink/exec).
Authorization floor rejects nested and *Authorized-suffixed forbidden trues; owner receipt correctly rejects taskId mismatch, target=master and any extra privilege.
append-only boundary library function is correct in isolation.
24/0 fixtures independently reproduced; node --check clean; workflow is read-only, credential-less, AI-free, non-merging, non-deploying, time-bounded.
Generated task is deterministic and complete with zero unresolved tokens and all authorizations false.
No research-ops-pilot/tasks mutation; no Binance pilot; master untouched.
correctionRequiredFindings: P1 --require-package CLI flag is not wired (parser key 'require-package' vs opts.requirePackage); it never forces the eleven-file package, so an empty skeleton passes with the flag.
P2 `validate` does not enforce state-to-evidence consistency; every evidence-bearing declared state passes with an empty package (only `status` catches it).
P3 Workflow is fail-open: `git fetch/diff ... || true` converts a discovery failure into an empty changed set and a PASS.
P4 Workflow silently skips deleted/absent task roots (`if [ -d "$t" ]`), so task-record deletion passes CI.
P5 Workflow does not enforce the append-only changed-file boundary (never invokes `validate --changed-files`).
P6 Canonical CLI `--tasks-dir` accepts absolute and `..` traversal paths, letting `create` write task skeletons outside `research-ops/tasks/`.
P7 Package validator does not reject nested subdirectories/files under `20-research-output/`.
P8 Package validator treats non-array/null reference fields as empty instead of flagging them.
P9 JSON schemas are documentation-only; malformed required shapes (missing `taskId`, IDENTITY/TASK_STATE `taskId` mismatch) pass validation.
nonblockingNotes: Authorization detection is heuristic (keys ending in `Authorized` plus known prefixes, recursively); arbitrary non-canonical names are not detected. No recognized authorization key escapes and owner-receipt escalation is fully rejected; recommend enumerating a canonical authorization key set.

FACTORY_STATE.json retains implementationCommitSha=null and exactImplementationFileCount=20; these are traceability notes only. The validated commit is unambiguously 02997bb and file counts reconcile (see packageFileBoundaryResult).
`status` does not verify 50/60/70/80 stage artifacts for declared states above PACKAGE_VALIDATED when a valid package exists.
An empty `20-research-output/` is not git-tracked until populated.
requiredCorrections: Wire `--require-package` to opts.requirePackage (alias fix) so it forces the eleven-file package check.
Make `validate` fail closed on declared-state-vs-evidence inconsistency (fold the status consistency gate into validate).
Remove/handle `|| true` in the workflow so a fetch/diff failure fails the job.
Make the workflow reject deletion/absence of a governed task root instead of skipping it.
Have the workflow build the PR changed-file list and run `validate --changed-files` to enforce the append-only boundary in CI.
Confine `--tasks-dir` to the repository `research-ops/tasks/` root (apply safeSubpath; reject absolute and `..` paths in `create`).
Reject unexpected subdirectories/files under `20-research-output/` in the package validator.
Flag non-array/null reference fields as invalid in cross-reference validation.
Add minimal structural enforcement (required keys incl. taskId; IDENTITY/TASK_STATE taskId consistency), or bind the schema files into the validator.
mergeReadiness: NOT_READY_FOR_OWNER_MERGE — the core architecture is usable, but the confirmed fail-open workflow behavior, the broken --require-package flag, the missing validate state/evidence gate, the un-enforced CI append-only boundary, and the CLI --tasks-dir path escape must be corrected before this becomes the canonical mechanism.
